What is eCommerce SEO?
attrs.html:
What is eCommerce SEO?

eCommerce SEO is the work that gets an online store’s category and product pages found in Google when shoppers search for what it sells. SEO for eCommerce websites covers the technical set-up of a large catalogue, the content on category and product pages, product schema for rich results, and links from other sites. Done well, it brings in shoppers who are ready to buy, without paying for every click. It rests on three things:

  1. 01

    Crawling and indexing

    Google can find, read and index the pages that matter, and ignores the thousands of filter and duplicate pages a store creates.

  2. 02

    Category and product pages

    Each page targets the words shoppers use, answers their questions and shows price, stock and reviews.

  3. 03

    Authority and rich results

    Links, reviews and product schema that earn trust, stars and prices in Google.

attrs.label: eCommerce SEO services that grow revenue
attrs.html:
eCommerce SEO services that grow revenue

Everything we handle for your store, and what you’ll see in your reports.

Fix what stops Google indexing your store

We clean up the filter, sort and duplicate pages that waste Google’s time, handle sold-out products properly and speed up mobile pages.

  • Faceted navigation and duplicates
  • Sold-out and discontinued products
  • Core Web Vitals and mobile speed

Common question

What is technical SEO for eCommerce?

It makes sure Google can crawl, index and understand a large catalogue. The usual fixes are filter and sort pages that create thousands of duplicates, sold-out products that return errors, slow mobile pages, and missing canonical tags. On most stores, fixing these lets the pages that matter rank before any new content is written.

Category pages that rank for the big searches

Category pages win the most valuable searches in a store. We give each one a clear target, a helpful intro, smart filters and answers to common questions.

  • One clear search per category
  • Short, helpful intros and FAQs
  • Links to guides and related categories

Common question

How do you optimise eCommerce category pages for SEO?

Give each category one clear search to target, a heading and title that use it, and a short, useful intro that helps shoppers choose. Link to related categories and buying guides, keep filters from creating indexable duplicates, and answer common questions on the page. Category pages usually win the highest-value searches in a store.

Product pages shoppers trust

We rewrite titles and descriptions for your priority products, and make price, stock, delivery and reviews easy to see.

  • Unique titles and descriptions
  • Reviews, stock and delivery shown clearly
  • Best-sellers and high-margin products first

Common question

How do you write product pages that rank?

Use the words shoppers search for in the title, write a unique description that answers real questions (size, material, delivery), and add reviews, clear prices and stock status. Avoid copying the manufacturer’s text. For large catalogues, start with your best-selling and highest-margin products.

Rich results that win the click

Product schema and a healthy Merchant Center feed make your products eligible for stars, prices and free listings in Google.

  • Product, offer and review schema
  • Shipping and returns details
  • Merchant Center feed checks

Common question

What is product schema, and does it help SEO?

Product schema is code that tells Google a page’s price, stock, rating, delivery and returns. It doesn’t lift rankings on its own, but it makes your listing eligible for rich results with stars and prices, and for free product listings, which usually means more clicks.

A structure Google and shoppers can follow

We plan clean URLs and a category structure that spreads authority to the pages that sell, and make sure no product is left orphaned.

  • Clean, readable URLs
  • Category hierarchy and breadcrumbs
  • Internal links to priority pages

Common question

What is the best URL structure for an eCommerce site?

Short, readable URLs that follow your categories, such as /dining/tables/ for a category and /products/oak-table/ for a product. Keep each product on one address, no matter which category it’s reached from, and make sure every product is linked from at least one category page.

Find the searches with buyers behind them

We find how shoppers describe your products, then map each search to one category or product page so your pages never compete.

  • Category and product searches
  • Questions shoppers ask before buying
  • Each search mapped to one page

Common question

How do you do keyword research for an eCommerce store?

Start with the products and categories you sell, then find how shoppers describe them: sizes, materials, styles and uses, such as “6 seater oak dining table”. Group similar searches so each one maps to a single category or product page, and pick the ones with buying intent first.

Buying guides that lead to products

Buying guides, size guides and comparisons bring in shoppers who are still deciding, then send them to the right products.

  • Buying and size guides
  • Comparisons and FAQs
  • Answers AI assistants can quote

Common question

Does an online store need a blog for SEO?

It needs helpful content more than a blog. Buying guides, size guides and comparisons answer the questions shoppers ask before they buy, and they link to the right products. They also give AI assistants and Google clear answers to quote, and earn links that lift your category pages.

Links from the sites your shoppers read

Gift guides, reviews, press mentions and partner listings that link to your category pages and build trust.

  • Gift guides and product reviews
  • Press and expert comments
  • No paid or spammy links

Common question

How do eCommerce sites get backlinks?

Through products and stories worth writing about: gift guides, product reviews, expert comments for the press, data from your own sales, and partners and suppliers who list you. A handful of relevant links to your category pages usually does more than many links to the homepage.

attrs.title: eCommerce SEO questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How much does eCommerce SEO cost?
items.answer: It depends on the size of your catalogue, your platform and how competitive your market is. We quote every eCommerce SEO package after a free call, so you only pay for what you need.

items.question: How long does eCommerce SEO take to work?
items.answer: Technical fixes can show results within weeks. Category pages usually climb over three to six months, depending on competition and how much the store needs.

items.question: Which eCommerce platform is best for SEO?
items.answer: Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento and BigCommerce can all rank well. What matters more is how the store is set up: clean URLs, controlled filters, fast pages and good content. We work with all of them, and with custom and headless stores.

items.question: What happens to SEO when a product sells out?
items.answer: If it’s coming back, keep the page live with a clear “back soon” message. If it’s gone for good, redirect it to the closest product or category, so you keep its rankings and links.

items.question: Should every product have a unique description?
items.answer: Your best-sellers and high-margin products should. For very large catalogues, we use smart templates for the rest and write unique copy where it pays back.

items.question: What is faceted navigation, and why does it matter for SEO?
items.answer: Faceted navigation is your filters, such as colour, size and price. Left alone, it can create thousands of near-duplicate pages. We decide which filters deserve to rank and keep the rest out of Google’s index.

items.question: Do you work with our in-house developers?
items.answer: Yes. We can brief your developers with clear tickets, or our own developers can make the changes on Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, BigCommerce and custom stores.

items.question: How do you measure eCommerce SEO results?
items.answer: Revenue and orders from organic search in Google Analytics, clicks and rankings in Search Console, and free listing performance in Merchant Center, reported monthly.

items.question: Do you offer eCommerce SEO consulting only?
items.answer: Yes. If you have your own team, a senior eCommerce SEO consultant can set the strategy, review work and guide your team each month.
